1.why: The UI uses a clean sans-serif typeface with adequate letter and line spacing across all screens.

2.why: Instructions use sentence case without italics or all-caps, though the demo info box and growing logs create some denser text blocks.

3.why: Layouts are single-column and appear usable at mobile width, with readable form fields and buttons.

4.why: Most instructions are short plain-language sentences such as 'Enter the six-digit code generated during setup'.

5.why: No explicit examples of expected input formats are shown beside fields (e.g., no sample code pattern near the authenticator or recovery inputs).

6.why: Core steps avoid long mandatory reading, but the persistent demo box and ever-expanding logs present sizable text the user must scroll past.

7.why: The manual setup secret and backup codes are displayed as selectable text so they can be copied, yet no dedicated copy button is provided.

8.why: Authenticator setup offers only manual secret entry; no QR code or equivalent alternative appears on any screen.

9.why: Standard email/phone inputs exist that browsers may autofill, but OTP and recovery-code fields show no explicit password-manager or one-time-code support.

10.why: Page titles and prominent blue primary buttons clearly indicate the current step and main action.

11.why: Each screen focuses on one primary task (verify identity, generate secret, confirm authenticator, save codes, etc.).

12.why: Green banners and status messages such as 'Setup secret generated' and 'Enrolment confirmed' plainly state what happened and the next step.

13.why: Users can re-request simulation challenges, navigate back to setup, and generate replacement backup codes without apparent penalty.

14.why: No error messages or validation failures are shown in the provided screenshots, so problem-and-fix language cannot be confirmed.

15.why: No countdown timers or reading/entry time limits are visible on any step of the flow.
